title: The group photo
logline: The mill's last-shift group photo, redrawn as a page: forty faces on the loading dock under the stack, Era I's black spotting brought back on purpose. Gully's uncle in the second row. A boy at the edge who might be anyone.

panels.composition: A group photograph as a drawing: forty men and a few women on a loading dock under the cedar mill's stack, 1994, in rows, the light flat, the line deliberately heavy with Era I's black spotting — every shadow a solid. In the second row, flat face, rain hood down: Gully's uncle, forty-something. At the far right edge, half cut off, a boy of thirteen or fourteen in a mill jacket too big for him, face turned away. A date scratched in the corner: '94.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no borders, heavy black ink spotting in a 1990s zine style over a muted ochre wash, a drawn group photograph of about forty mill workers in rows on a loading dock beneath a tall smokestack, one weathered man in the second row with a rain hood down, a half-cut-off teenage boy at the far right edge with his face turned away, no words
image.notes: The boy at the edge is reserved. Draw him turned away. Era I's spotting on purpose — the only sequence where the old line returns.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: Forty faces. The uncle. The boy at the edge, reserved.
